source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Electrical - Body and Chassis, p.12-48

procedures.title: Wiper motor brush plate and circuit breaker: remove (Type C depressed park wiper)
steps: Scribe a line along the side of the casting and end cap for reassembly.
Push the spare motor lead length through the casting grommet and ease the case, field and armature away from the casting (see figure 71 in the manual).
Unsolder the black lead from the circuit breaker (see figure 72 in the manual).
Straighten the 4 tabs holding the brush plate to the field coil retainers, without breaking any.
Fit a U-shaped retainer clip over the brush holder whose lead goes to the circuit breaker (see figure 73 in the manual).
Hold the opposite brush and lift the brush holder off its tabs just far enough to clear the commutator.
Let that brush come out of its holder, remove the brush spring and lift the holder off the armature shaft.
notes: Manual lists the Type C depressed park wiper for Chevelle, Chevrolet and Corvette.

Type C: blades park against the lower windshield molding; 12-volt compound-wound motor with a worm driving the main gear and crank arm; a relay coil, armature and switch in the gear box control start and stop through a latch; an electric washer pump on the gear box is driven by the wiper gear. Motor, gear box and washer pump can each be serviced on their own.
The motor section can be taken apart without disturbing the gear box.
If needed, remove the armature end play adjusting screw and push a rod through the hole against the armature end.

procedures.title: Wiper armature: remove (Type C depressed park wiper)
steps: Do brush plate removal steps 1 through 8.
Lift the armature out of the case and field.
Remove the thrust ball from the shaft end if needed and keep it; a magnet picks it up easily.
